subject: Literacy
title: Two-step instructions
subtopics: Giving an instruction to a friend
objectives: Children will follow a two-part instruction.
Children will give a simple instruction to a friend.
content: Following one-step and two-step instructions and giving a simple instruction to a friend.
teachingActivities: Give one instruction at a time first; use the words first and then; show with actions and wait before repeating; use real objects; never rush a child who needs time to think.
learnerActivities: Follow a two-part instruction and give a simple instruction to a friend.
resources: A ball, a cup, a spoon and a teddy
assessment: Observe whether each child follows a two-step instruction and gives a one-step instruction.
crossCurricular: Social Habits: listening and following directions

lessons.title: One thing at a time
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will follow a one-step instruction such as "Bring me the ball".
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow one-step instructions, hear the sounds s, a, t and p and answer simple questions.
resources: A ball, a cup, a spoon and a teddy
lessons.starter: Say "Listen, then do. Bring me the ball." Wait and look at the children.
teacherActivities: Say "Bring me the ball" and show a hand gesture. Wait for a child to bring it.
Say "Put the cup in the basket." Show the basket.
Give instructions to each child with a different object.
Praise each child by saying what they did.
learnerActivities: Child brings the ball.
Child puts the cup in the basket.
Child listens and does the action.
Child smiles and shows what they did.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say "Bring me the ball" and show a hand gesture. Wait for a child to bring it. Children: Child brings the ball.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Put the cup in the basket." Show the basket. Children: Child puts the cup in the basket.
Step 3. Teacher: Give instructions to each child with a different object. Children: Child listens and does the action.
Step 4. Teacher: Praise each child by saying what they did. Children: Child smiles and shows what they did.

practical.title: Listen and do
steps: Put four objects on the mat.
Give each child a one-step instruction.
Say well done and put the object back.
practical.safety: Keep objects soft and safe and the floor clear. Do not rush the child and repeat the instruction once calmly.

differentiation.support: Point to the object and say the instruction slowly.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to give a friend an instruction.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you bring me the ball?
Where did you put the cup?

lessons.conclusion: Put the objects away and say "Good listening."
lessons.homeConnection: Give your child one-step instructions at home such as "Put your shoes here".
teacherReflection: Which children could show "follow a one-step instruction such as "Bring me the ball"" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: First and then
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will follow a two-part instruction with first and then.
successCriteria: Does both parts of the instruction
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow one-step instructions, hear the sounds s, a, t and p and answer simple questions.
resources: A ball, a cup and a basket
lessons.starter: Say "First clap, then stamp." Do it slowly and show the order with fingers: one, two.
teacherActivities: Say "First clap, then stamp" and do the actions with the children.
Say "First touch your head, then touch your toes."
Say "First pick up the ball, then put it in the basket."
Let each child have a turn with a new instruction.
learnerActivities: Children clap and then stamp.
Children touch their head, then their toes.
Child does both actions in order.
Child listens and does both parts.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say "First clap, then stamp" and do the actions with the children. Children: Children clap and then stamp.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "First touch your head, then touch your toes." Children: Children touch their head, then their toes.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "First pick up the ball, then put it in the basket." Children: Child does both actions in order.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child have a turn with a new instruction. Children: Child listens and does both parts.

practical.title: Two things
steps: Put a ball, a cup and a basket on the mat.
The child does both parts in order.
practical.safety: Keep the instructions simple and the space clear. If the child forgets, repeat gently and help with a gesture.

differentiation.support: Show the first action, wait, then show the second.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to remember three things in order.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Say "First tidy up, then sit down" and do it together.
lessons.homeConnection: Give two-part instructions at home such as "First wash hands, then eat".
teacherReflection: Which children could show "follow a two-part instruction with first and then" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Go and bring
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will go to a place and bring back an object.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow one-step instructions, hear the sounds s, a, t and p and answer simple questions.
lessons.starter: Say "Go to the box, then bring me the teddy." Point to the box.
teacherActivities: Give the instruction and let one child try while others watch.
Change the instruction: "Go to the table, then bring the spoon."
Let each child have a turn with a new instruction.
Praise each child by saying what they did.
learnerActivities: Child goes to the box and brings the teddy.
Child goes to the table and brings the spoon.
Child goes and brings an object.
Child smiles and shows what they brought.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Give the instruction and let one child try while others watch. Children: Child goes to the box and brings the teddy.
Step 2. Teacher: Change the instruction: "Go to the table, then bring the spoon." Children: Child goes to the table and brings the spoon.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child have a turn with a new instruction. Children: Child goes and brings an object.
Step 4. Teacher: Praise each child by saying what they did. Children: Child smiles and shows what they brought.

practical.title: Fetch game
steps: Put four objects in different places.
Give each child a go-and-bring instruction.
The child goes and brings the object back.
practical.safety: Keep the objects within easy reach and the path clear. Walk, do not run, and supervise movement.

differentiation.support: Walk with the child and point at the object.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to bring two objects in one trip.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Where did you go?
questions.expected: To the box or the table.

expectedOutcomes: Goes and brings an object on instruction
lessons.conclusion: Put the objects back in the right places.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child to go and bring something, such as "Go to the kitchen and bring a spoon".
teacherReflection: Which children could show "go to a place and bring back an object" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: I am the leader
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: Giving an instruction to a friend
objectives: Children will give a simple instruction to a friend.
successCriteria: Says an instruction to a friend
Waits for the friend to do it
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow one-step instructions, hear the sounds s, a, t and p and answer simple questions.
resources: A ball, a cup and a basket
lessons.starter: Put on the leader’s hat and say "I am the leader. Bring me the cup." Give the hat to a child.
teacherActivities: Show how to be a leader: say "Clap" and everyone claps.
Give the hat to a child and help them say an instruction.
Let the friend follow the instruction.
Swap the hat and let others be the leader.
learnerActivities: Children clap on the instruction.
Child says an instruction such as "clap".
Friend does what the leader says.
Child leads and friends follow.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to be a leader: say "Clap" and everyone claps. Children: Children clap on the instruction.
Step 2. Teacher: Give the hat to a child and help them say an instruction. Children: Child says an instruction such as "clap".
Step 3. Teacher: Let the friend follow the instruction. Children: Friend does what the leader says.
Step 4. Teacher: Swap the hat and let others be the leader. Children: Child leads and friends follow.

practical.title: Leader game
steps: Choose a leader with the hat.
The leader tells a friend what to do.
Swap the hat and play again.
practical.safety: Keep instructions kind and safe. Do not allow instructions that could hurt a friend and supervise each pair.

differentiation.support: Whisper the instruction to the leader and let them say it.
differentiation.extension: Ask the leader to give a two-part instruction.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Gives a simple instruction to a friend
lessons.conclusion: Give the hat back and say "Well done, leaders."
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child give you an instruction and follow it.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "give a simple instruction to a friend" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 6 instructions check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child follows and gives instructions.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow one-step instructions, hear the sounds s, a, t and p and answer simple questions.
lessons.starter: Say "First listen, then do" and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: one-step, two-step and leader.
At each station give an instruction and watch.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child does the action.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: one-step, two-step and leader. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station give an instruction and watch. Children: Child does the action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Instruction stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use soft objects only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one-step instructions.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to give a two-step instruction.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: follows one-step instructions; follows two-step instructions; gives an instruction to a friend.

questions.question: What do you do first?
questions.expected: The first part of the instruction.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 6
lessons.homeConnection: Practise first and then at home with small tasks.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child follows and gives instructions" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
